elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Client owns “all deliverables ... created for Client under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Client owns all “work product created for Client under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Vendor assigns all deliverables created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: TrueLink “hereby assigns such deliverables ... to Client,” effecting a present assignment.

elements.element: Vendor assigns all work product created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: TrueLink “hereby assigns such ... work product to Client,” effecting a present assignment.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all Vendor pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: TrueLink retains rights in the Interface, but there is no general retention or carve-out covering all pre-existing TrueLink IP, tools or materials. The reference to embedded TrueLink IP shows that Vendor IP may extend beyond the Interface.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: TrueLink grants Client a licence to “any TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in such deliverables and work product.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly “perpetual.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Client expressly retains “all right, title and interest” in Client Content and Credit Data, the customer-data categories identified in the clause.

elements.element: No intellectual property is jointly owned by Customer and Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that no intellectual property will be jointly owned by the parties.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause preserves TrueLink's rights only in the Interface; it does not reserve the broader category of generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: There is no operative reservation of TrueLink's know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives rights in the deliverables equivalent to a licence.
elements.evidence: Client receives outright ownership through a present assignment, which is broader than a licence as to the assigned deliverable IP; embedded TrueLink IP is separately licensed.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: The assignment contains no reversion or time limit, and the licence for embedded TrueLink IP is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The ownership assignment is not stated to be revocable, and the embedded-IP licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: No worldwide scope is stated for the embedded TrueLink IP licence, so worldwide exploitation of deliverables containing that IP is not assured.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty applies to the assigned deliverables, and the embedded-IP licence is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the deliverables permits Client to use them, and the unqualified licence to embedded TrueLink IP supports use of that embedded IP.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Although Client owns the assigned work product, the licence to embedded TrueLink IP does not expressly permit modification, so modification of the deliverables as a whole is not assured.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The embedded TrueLink IP licence contains no sublicensing right; a nonexclusive licence is not ordinarily sublicensable without express language.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its rights in the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The assigned ownership and embedded-IP licence contain no field-of-use restriction and therefore cover Client's business use.

result.reason: The redline substantially implements the preferred customer-ownership position, but it does not generally reserve all Vendor pre-existing IP; retaining rights only in the Interface is too narrow. The fallback also fails because generic tools and know-how are not broadly reserved and the embedded-IP licence lacks express worldwide, modification and sublicensing rights. The redline is not minimal and does not preserve the original commercial allocation because it separately deletes TrueLink's rights to distribute, disseminate, license, resell and exploit Credit Data, a material change not required merely to allocate ownership. Drafting is otherwise reasonably clear, but repeated subsection lettering, undefined IP terminology and the malformed Credit Data definition reduce quality.
